description: ASTRAVIGIL is a student-led project focused on astronaut health monitoring during space missions. We are interested in biotechnology, biomedical research, data analysis and space science. Our goal is to explore NASA research datasets and develop an accessible prototype for visualizing astronaut health indicators. We welcome collaborators with skills in Python, programming, UI/UX design, data science and biomedical research.
summary:
ASTRAVIGIL is a research-based astronaut health monitoring prototype designed to explore biochemical health changes during space missions. Using NASA's OSD-575 Comprehensive Metabolic Panel (CMP) dataset, we developed an interactive dashboard that visualizes 19 blood chemistry analytes across pre-flight and post-flight timepoints for four participants.

The prototype provides participant-level trends, group averages, and reference-range screening to help users explore changes in measurements such as glucose, creatinine, sodium and potassium. It aims to make astronaut biomedical research data easier to understand and explore, supporting future approaches to mission health monitoring.

ASTRAVIGIL demonstrates how space research datasets can be transformed into accessible, data-driven health visualization tools. It is a research prototype, not a live medical monitoring or diagnostic system.
details: ASTRAVIGIL is a mobile-first research prototype designed to help astronauts and mission teams explore health-related information relevant to long-duration spaceflight. It organizes information into cardiovascular, bone and muscle, radiation, and wellbeing modules, with a NASA research-study explorer. The current prototype references NASA OSDR study OSD-575, which contains pre-flight and post-flight blood-serum metabolic and immune/cardiovascular biomarker research from the Inspiration4 crew. It presents study context, sample timelines, assay information, and data provenance in an accessible interface. The project was developed as a lightweight web application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, with a focus on mobile usability, clear navigation, and scientific transparency. It distinguishes published research metadata from live sensor measurements and does not claim to provide real-time astronaut monitoring, automated diagnosis, or validated medical alerts. ASTRAVIGIL aims to demonstrate how accessible research tools can support exploration of astronaut health evidence and inform future health-monitoring software.
